He played for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball]] team from 2008 to 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/kris-joseph |title=Kris Joseph |publisher=NBADraft.net |date=June 24, 2009 |access-date=October 25, 2012}} He was selected in the second round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 51st pick overall. He is the older cousin of Pistons point guard [[Cory Joseph]]. ==Early years== Joseph was born and raised in [[Montreal]], Quebec, where he grew up in the working-class neighbourhood of [[Cote-des-Neiges]] north of downtown. Joseph first picked up a basketball in Grade 2 but was forced to shoot on garbage cans with his older brother Maurice. A court was eventually erected in Cote-des-Neiges and the brothers battled for hours.{{cite web |url=http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=755 |title=Welcome |publisher=QHoops |access-date=October 25, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131217221546/http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=755 |archive-date=December 17, 2013 }} ==High school career== Joseph played in Maurice's shadow for a number of years as the older star gained prominence at noted Montreal-area prep school Champlain St. Lambert College.{{cite web |url=http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=734 |title=Welcome |publisher=QHoops |date=March 17, 2005 |access-date=October 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051226195514/http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=734 |archive-date=December 26, 2005 |url-status=dead }} Kris struggled at first against elite competition, getting cut from his club team at the age of 14. He worked on his game, grew to 6-foot-6 and became a star for Sun Youth, a club-team powerhouse in the Montreal Basketball League. As a tenth-grader, he led the Quebec provincial team to a silver medal at the 2005 Canada Games. He played for his high school team at Mont-Royal high school, the Mount-Royal Mustangs.{{cite web |url=https://montreal.ctvnews.ca/montreal-s-joseph-brothers-to-battle-on-grand-stage-1.493467 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120711162919/http://montreal.ctvnews.ca/montreal-s-joseph-brothers-to-battle-on-grand-stage-1.493467 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 11, 2012 |title=Montreal's Joseph brothers to battle on grand stage | CTV Montreal News |publisher=Montreal.ctv.ca |date=March 18, 2010 |access-date=October 25, 2012 }} On a recommendation from youth coach Henry Wong, who thought Joseph needed an athletic and academic challenge, Joseph's mother agreed to let him leave Montreal in 2006 to complete two years of high school at Archbishop Carroll in Washington, D.C.{{cite web|author1=Dennis Nett |author2=The Post-Standard |url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2012/03/kris_joseph_road_winds_from_mo.html |title=Kris Joseph: Road winds from Montreal to D.C. to Syracuse | syracuse.com |date=March 2, 2012 |publisher=Blog.syracuse.com |access-date=October 25, 2012}} As a senior, Joseph led Archbishop Carroll to a 26–11 record, including a 21-point, five rebound, three assist and three block effort in the Washington Catholic Athletic Conference (WCAC) Tournament in a 65–55 win over Our Lady of Good Counsel. Joseph was also invited to play in the Baltimore All-Stars vs. U.S. All-Stars Exhibition in April. That season, Joseph would go on to earn 2008 second team honors from the [[Washington Post]].{{cite web |url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=2692&sport=176&roster=228&path=mbasket |title=Syracuse University Athletics - TEMP 2009-10 Signing Day 2010 Roster |publisher=Suathletics.com |access-date=October 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081230150143/http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=2692&sport=176&roster=228&path=mbasket |archive-date=December 30, 2008 |url-status=dead }} He played [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball with the DC Assault. Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Joseph was listed as the No. 17 small forward and the No. 113 player in the nation in 2008.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Kris-Joseph-60727;_ylt=AoUmdPN6wLDrJoIHTS3Ie11GPZB4 Kris Joseph Recruiting Profile] ==College career== ===2008–09=== Joseph would see early playing time, including seven points in 22 minutes in an 85–51 rout of [[Le Moyne College|Le Moyne]] on November 16, 2008 {{Cite web|url=http://www.auburnpub.com/articles/2008/11/17/sports/sports05.txt|title = Orange roll past le Moyne | date=November 17, 2008 }} and a 13-point six rebound effort in an 86–66 victory against Oakland University on November 22, 2008.{{cite web|url=http://www.democratandchronicle.com/article/20081122/SPORTS09/811220326/1007/SPORTS |title=College Sports |publisher=Democrat and Chronicle |access-date=July 16, 2013}} On November 24, 2008, Joseph's 10 points and five rebounds helped then-unranked Syracuse upset then-No. 18 Florida, 89–83, in the semi-finals of the [[CBE Classic]].{{cite web|author=Sprint Center, Kansas City, MO |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=283290183 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Florida Gators - Box Score - November 24, 2008 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=November 24, 2008 |access-date=October 25, 2012}} After an injury to [[Paul Harris (basketball)|Paul Harris]], Joseph would receive the first start of his career against [[South Florida University|South Florida]] on January 2, 2009, scoring seven points and adding three rebounds.{{cite web|author=Central New York |url=http://www.syracuse.com/axeman/index.ssf/2009/01/susouth_florida_recap_1.html |title=SU-South Florida Recap |date=January 3, 2009 |publisher=syracuse.com |access-date=October 25, 2012}} ===2009–10=== Joseph would become a key reserve in his second year at Syracuse. In SU's [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]] opener against [[Seton Hall University|Seton Hall]] on December 29, 2009, Joseph scored 16 points, including 8-of-9 shooting from the free throw line in an 80–73 win.{{cite web|author=Prudential Center, Newark, NJ |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=293642550 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Seton Hall Pirates - Box Score - December 29, 2009 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=December 29, 2009 |access-date=October 25, 2012}} On January 6, 2010, against Memphis, Joseph scored 15 second half points to go along with nine rebounds in a 74–57 win.{{cite web|author=Carrier Dome, Syracuse, NY |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=300070183 |title=Memphis Tigers vs. Syracuse Orange - Box Score - January 06, 2010 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 6, 2010 |access-date=October 25, 2012}} Joseph finished with averages of 11.0 points and 5.4 rebounds on the season, and was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Big East Conference Sixth Man of the Year]].{{cite web |url=http://suathletics.syr.edu/news/2010/3/8/JosephBE3.8.10.aspx |title=Syracuse University Athletics - Joseph Earns BIG EAST Sixth Man Award |publisher=Suathletics.syr.edu |access-date=October 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120811055618/http://suathletics.syr.edu/news/2010/3/8/JosephBE3.8.10.aspx |archive-date=August 11, 2012 |url-status=dead }} ===2010–11=== Joseph gained national prominence as a go-to scorer for the Orange during his junior year. He was named in the Wooden Award Preseason Top 50 list and improved his numbers across the board, leading Syracuse in scoring at 14.3 points per game and placing second in rebounding (5.2) and steals (1.5). He was named to the All-Big East third team, the first Canadian to receive the honour since fellow Montrealer [[Bill Wennington]] in 1985.{{cite web |url=http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/100511aaa.html |title=St. John's Bill Wennington To Be Inducted Into Quebec Sports Hall of Fame - ST. JOHN'S UNIVERSITY OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=Redstormsports.com |date=October 5, 2011 |access-date=October 25, 2012 |archive-date=March 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325220427/http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/100511aaa.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=http://suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7750&path=mbasket |title=Syracuse University Athletics - 2011-12 Men's Basketball Roster |publisher=Suathletics.com |access-date=October 25, 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.qhoops.net/articles/article.jsp?aId=1341 |title=Welcome |publisher=QHoops |date=March 22, 2011 |access-date=October 25, 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=February 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ===2011–12=== Joseph was once again named to the Wooden Award Preseason Top 50 list as a senior.{{cite web|url=http://suathletics.com/news/2011/11/7/MBB_1107113314.aspx?path=mbasket |title=Syracuse University Athletics - Joseph on Naismith Watch List |publisher=Suathletics.com |date=November 7, 2011 |access-date=October 25, 2012}} His final season started off with a flourish as he was named the Big East Player of the Week after leading his Syracuse Orange to the NIT Season Tip Off Championship. Joseph was named Most Outstanding Player of the tournament with averages of 19.0 points, 9.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals in wins against Virginia Tech and Stanford.{{cite web|url=http://suathletics.com/news/2011/11/25/MBB_1125110943.aspx?path=mbasket |title=Syracuse University Athletics - #5/5 Syracuse Wins NIT Season Tip Off |publisher=Suathletics.com |date=November 25, 2011 |access-date=October 25, 2012}} He led the Orange in scoring during the regular season (13.4 ppg) and received an array of post-season awards, including a spot on the 2012 All-Big East First Team. Joseph is the first Canadian-born player ever to be named to the first team of that conference.{{cite web|last=Daly |first=Brian |url=http://www.torontosun.com/2012/03/04/joseph-makes-history-with-big-east-nod |title=Joseph makes history with Big East nod | Basketball | Sports |publisher=Toronto Sun |date=March 4, 2012 |access-date=October 25, 2012}} He was named an AP Honorable Mention All-American {{cite web|author=CBSSports.com wire reports |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/18064597/ap-allamerica-teams |title=2012 AP All-America teams - NCAA Division I Mens Basketball - CBSSports.com News, Scores, Stats, Schedule and RPI Rankings |publisher=Cbssports.com |access-date=July 16, 2013}} and also earned spots on the USBWA All District II team as well as the NABC All-District 5 First Team. Additionally, Joseph was one of 15 post-season finalists for the Wooden Award, making him among the most decorated Canadians ever to play NCAA Division I basketball. With his 15 points against Manhattan on November 14, 2011, Joseph became the 55th player at Syracuse to score 1,000 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7750&path=mbasket |title=Syracuse University Athletics - Kris Joseph - 2011-12 Men's Basketball |publisher=Suathletics.com |access-date=July 16, 2013}} He concluded his storied career with 10 points, two rebounds and 3 steals in Syracuse's 77–70 loss to Ohio State in the Elite Eight. ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics=== Joseph was selected in the second round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 51st pick. On July 3, 2012, Joseph signed a contract with the Celtics.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press070312-celtics-sign-2012-draft-picks.html|title=Celtics Sign 2012 NBA Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 4, 2012|date=July 3, 2012}} On July 5, 2012, the [[Boston Celtics]] announced that Joseph was added to their roster for the 2012 [[Orlando Summer League|Orlando]] and [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas]] NBA Summer League's.{{cite web|last=Rohrbach |first=Ben |url=http://www.weei.com/sports/boston/this-just-in/21211731/rookies-williams-cs-summer-league-roster |title=Sean Williams on C's summer league roster |publisher=Weei.com |access-date=July 16, 2013}} On October 24, Kris Joseph officially made the Celtics' 15-man roster. He was sent to the [[Maine Red Claws]] of the [[NBA D-League]][http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/celtics_assign_firstround_pick_melo_second_round_pick_joseph_to_red_claws_2012_11_14.html Melo, Joseph assigned to D-League] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119050548/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/celtics_assign_firstround_pick_melo_second_round_pick_joseph_to_red_claws_2012_11_14.html |date=November 19, 2015 }} for several assignments during his time with the Celtics.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html 2012-13 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |date=March 27, 2014 }} On January 6, 2013, he was waived by the 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on April 2, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-kris-joseph-10-day-contract |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Kris Joseph to 10-Day Contract |work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=April 2, 2013 |access-date=April 12, 2013}} On April 12, 2013, he was signed for the remainder of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-kris-joseph-remainder-season |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Kris Joseph for Remainder of Season |work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=April 12, 2013 |access-date=April 12, 2013}} Joseph was traded back to his draft team the [[Boston Celtics]] on July 12, 2013, along with [[Keith Bogans]], [[Kris Humphries]], [[MarShon Brooks]] and [[Gerald Wallace]] as well as three first-round picks in a blockbuster deal that sent Celtics stars [[Kevin Garnett]], [[Paul Pierce]] and [[Jason Terry]] to the Nets. It was the first time two players named Kris were traded with each other.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-complete-trade-brooklyn-nets|title=Celtics Complete Trade With Brooklyn Nets|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=July 12, 2013}} He was one of two players traded to the team that originally drafted them: Joseph was drafted by Boston in 2012 and Brooks was drafted by Boston in the [[2011 NBA draft]].
